utterances.text: It's at page 89. What appears in my LiveNote as lines 11 down through to, I think, page 90 line 3. It takes -- there Dr. Karadzic specifically referred to a specific article on a specific date in a specific newspaper and told the witness the specific page exactly what she said. That would clearly go to identify her. But it was difficult to find that article without any 65 ter number being quoted or Defence-released document, so I apologise for the time it took me. So I'd like that redacted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Specifically what lines?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: It's a bit confusing in the LiveNote, but it reads -- my page 89 at LiveNote stops at line 12, so it's the question that begins at page 89, line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you -- starting with "Did you correct that in" - certain number of the magazine - "Oslobodjenje?" If you could read out the passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: The passage that I think goes to identify this witness is: "And another statement says, this is commission of experts, the" -- I'm sorry, "the interviews from 1994 and page 8 you said it was on your [sic] face." Sorry, I've just found it. Thank you. "However, in "Oslobodjenje" ... on the 6th of August, 1997, on page 8, you said ... it was on the breast." So both of those things, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And then further down it -- the witness -- the accused asked "Did you correct that in "Oslobodjenje?" And then witness answered, referring to that article. Is it okay? Unless it refers to the specific issue of that magazine, or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I think with the initial redaction, that second passage is actually okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. We go back to open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, may I know if I get any more time tomorrow and how much? There is a large topic that still have to go through and I've barely touched upon several other subjects, especially where personalities and specific incidents are concerned. I need, if not a whole session, then at least an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think so, but I will let you know in a couple of minutes. In the meantime, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's -- this is certainly safe to say. Was your position and your institution of municipal nature?

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if a Muslim municipality had been formed, the same institution would have existed in it?

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: How could I know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, in Sarajevo, which has ten municipalities, does every municipality have that same kind of institution?

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: But they're not Muslim institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that when a municipality exists, it has that institution.

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that it had been offered to the Muslims and Croats working in state administration to pledge an oath to the Serb authorities or to move to a Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Prijedor, Muslims and Croats received an offer to make an oath that they will enforce the laws of the -- of Republika Srpska, and some did, whereas others were waiting for a Muslim municipality to be formed. Do you know that there was this oath of loyalty, a solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: KDZ080
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that, but one woman inmate told us that she had signed some sort of document on loyalty. She was working in that -- in a centre in Sarajevo, and she was still brought to the camp. Another woman didn't sign and was brought to the camp too. So I don't know if it had anything to do with it, this signing of loyalty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we will adjourn for today here, and you'll have 25 minutes tomorrow to conclude your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll resume tomorrow at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can just raise something in relation to the supplemental motion that was filed in the break. We would ask that the appendixes still remain confidential because the address of the witness is in there and also security concerns on matters which are normally dealt with in confidential filings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And with respect --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And also for the 61st motion as well, if those appendices could also be put under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, Mr. President, we would be happy to redact any address. But in terms of the other information, we don't think it should be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll take a look into.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But, sorry, Your Honour, at the moment they're a public document, until you rule otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I meant that we'll put it under seal provisionally and we'll take a look, further look.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And with respect to Mr. Robinson's request to lift the confidentiality of the Chamber's ruling, with respect to this witness, we agree that this can be -- the confidentiality of the ruling can be lifted. But except for the last passage which relates to the warning to the witness, so, i.e., the -- from my transcript page -- on page -- line 21 of page 52 to 24 -- and line 24, transcript page 53, can be public. Very well. I always forget to mention the audio/video part as well. The hearing is now adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th day of October, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.
